title: Invocation is the chief part: Saints as guardians who hear even silent prayers
source_text: VIII. Sed praecipuam partem cultus qui Sanctis exhiberi solet positam esse docuimus in eorum invocatione, per quam Sanctorum in Christo defunctorum opem & auxilium, privatim & publice implorant: supponentes eos non tantum in genere pro Ecclesia Militante, sed etiam pro singulis fidelibus intercedere; quin eos constitutos esse generis humani custodes, patronos, atque protectores, qui singulorum necessitates, non solum videre possint, verum etiam preces solo corde conceptas audire.
pass_a_gloss: But we taught that the chief part of the cult usually shown to the Saints is placed in their invocation, by which people privately and publicly implore the help and aid of the Saints who have died in Christ: supposing that they intercede not only in general for the Church Militant but also for individual believers; indeed that they are appointed guardians, patrons, and protectors of the human race, who can not only see the needs of each person but also hear prayers conceived in the heart alone.
pass_b_english: The main Roman act toward the Saints is calling on them, in private and in public.
They are supposed to intercede for the Church at large and for each believer.
They are treated as guardians who see each person's need and hear prayers that are never spoken aloud.

lemmas.gloss: prayers conceived by the heart alone

choices.why: States the office Rome assigns, beyond mere memory of the dead.
